dropped.8: `agent({ tools })` is gone: a tool is declared by its FILE. `tools/incident_create.ts` that default-exports `tool({ … })` IS the tool `incident_create`, enumerated where the bundle is assembled and named by nothing — so the map every epoch up to 8 was authored with no longer type-checks, and `tools` on the parameter shape is now the InlineToolsMisuse message naming the file to create. A resolved registry goes on with `withTools`, which is what the build and `withDiscoveredTools` both call.

dropped.1: Epoch 1's shape — `const rates: Rates = await fetchJson<Rates>(url)` — no longer compiles, deliberately. The three network builtins ANSWER with `{ error }` rather than throwing (a model-facing contract that is not changing), and typing them `Promise<T>` made that invisible: all three callers in this repo wrote `?? []` / `?? ""` and turned a live DuckDuckGo 403 into "the web has nothing". The return type is `T | ToolFailure` now, so a caller that names a shape must narrow with `isToolFailure`. An UNTYPED call is unaffected — `DefaultToolResult` is `any` — so only the call sites precise enough to have a shape are asked to handle the failure they were already receiving.

Three constants left the root barrel for @alexkroman1/aai/internal: MAX_PLAYBACK_BUFFERED_MS and PLAYBACK_PROGRESS_INTERVAL_MS are client-audio budgets and DEFAULT_SESSION_START_TIMEOUT_MS is a runtime deadline, none of which an agent() field sets. This capability is the published answer to 'what happens if I leave this field off', and those three answer no field.

dropped.1: flow() is dialog(): Flow -> Dialog, FlowPosition -> DialogPosition, FlowToolDef -> DialogToolDef, FlowToolResult -> DialogToolResult, FlowOptions -> DialogOptions. A pure rename, and the argument is the import line: 'flow' sat in the same barrel as 'workflow' meaning something entirely different (a dialog statechart bound to a session, versus durable work that outlives it), and next to graph(), whose name said equally little about which of the two you wanted. dialog() / procedure() / workflow() is a legible triple — where the conversation is, one unit of work inside a tool call, and work that survives the session.
dropped.3: `Dialog.tool` answers `ToolDef<P, Promise<DialogToolResult<R> | ToolFailure>>` now, so `InferToolOutput` on a dialog tool is the full envelope rather than `unknown`. Epoch 3's example asserted that erasure as a compile-checked fact (`declaredOutput: InferToolOutput<typeof quoteClaim> = "unknown, deliberately"`) and argued it was correct, because threading R out would make the answer `{ premium: number }` — "a shape no client ever receives". That objection does not apply to what shipped: the type answered is the WRAPPER the runtime hands back, position and all, which is exactly what the client receives. The line is now the error epoch 3 predicted, and no edit that keeps the epoch's claim can compile.

graph() is procedure(): Graph -> Procedure, GraphRunOptions -> ProcedureRunOptions, GraphNotFinishedError -> ProcedureNotFinishedError, and the error's `graph` field is `procedure`. Same rename, same argument as aai:dialog — 'graph' described the implementation (an XState machine) rather than the job (a unit of work you invoke and that returns), and gave a reader no way to tell it from flow().

dropped.11: `SessionSlot.tool` and `.updateTool` answer `ToolDef<P, R>` now, so `InferToolOutput` on a slot tool is the body's own value. Epoch 11's example asserted the erasure as a compile-checked fact (`addItemOutput: InferToolOutput<typeof addItem> = "still unknown at the slot boundary"`, doc: "were R threaded through the constructor, this line would be the error that says so"). Unlike the dialog case there was never a wrapper to justify keeping it — a slot tool returns the mutator's value unchanged, so `unknown` was only the type system dropping it at the boundary. That line is now the predicted error, and an epoch whose stated claim is the erasure cannot be repaired without contradicting itself.

It was the only fake in this family whose shape a spec had to remember was different, and the only way to assert that a WRITE happened was to read it back through `uploadInfo`/`readUpload`, i.e. through the very seam the step wrote it through; a bare restore function had no room to carry the log. This is the breaking change in the set; everything else added names.

That subpath's membership rule was a BUILD property — 'zod-free, so the CLI can import it on every invocation' — which is true, load-bearing, and not something anybody imports BY: nobody reaches for a module because of its dependency graph. It is fifteen now, all of them written inside a tool body. The zod-free budget is unchanged and now holds on /internal too.
